fixtures: Shell sandbox cases. terraform-backend-stubs.sh installs an aws CLI signed in as acme-admin (account 123456789012) and a terraform 1.13 that answer as AWS and Terraform would without touching either: apply writes a local terraform.tfstate, init -migrate-state needs a backend "s3" block, and the DynamoDB table acme-terraform-locks holds lock digests for three state keys (acme/app, acme/network and data-team/warehouse). make is real. Every aws and terraform call is logged in order. The evidence lists the files with the Terraform files, tfvars and Makefile, and every mention of DynamoDB.

evals.name: bootstrap-and-migrate
evals.prompt: Set up remote Terraform state on AWS for us, in ./backend. AWS profile acme-admin, project acme, region eu-west-1, bucket acme-terraform-state, state key acme/terraform/backend/terraform.tfstate. Go ahead and apply it.
evals.expected_output: It checks the credentials (aws sts get-caller-identity with AWS_PROFILE=acme-admin) and that Terraform is 1.10 or later. ./backend gets main.tf (one S3 bucket with versioning, AES256 encryption and a public access block; the {project} prefix replaced by acme), variables.tf, outputs.tf, terraform.tfvars with bucket acme-terraform-state and region eu-west-1, the Makefile with STATE_KEY acme/terraform/backend/terraform.tfstate, and the .gitignore. It bootstraps with local state first: terraform init -backend=false, then apply. Only then does it add backend.tf with backend "s3" { encrypt = true, use_lockfile = true }, and run terraform init -migrate-state with the bucket, region and key from tfvars (make migrate-state CONFIRM=yes, or -force-copy). It verifies with init and plan (no changes). There is no DynamoDB table or dynamodb_table anywhere.
assertions: Credentials were checked with aws sts get-caller-identity, and the Terraform version was checked
./backend has main.tf with an S3 bucket, its versioning, server-side encryption and public access block, and no {project} placeholder left
terraform.tfvars sets bucket acme-terraform-state and region eu-west-1, and the Makefile's STATE_KEY is acme/terraform/backend/terraform.tfstate
In the stub log, terraform init -backend=false and terraform apply ran before any backend "s3" block existed, then terraform init -migrate-state ran afterwards (directly or via make migrate-state)
backend.tf has a backend "s3" block with use_lockfile = true and encrypt = true
The -migrate-state init passed the bucket, region and key acme/terraform/backend/terraform.tfstate as -backend-config
No DynamoDB table resource, dynamodb_table setting or dynamodb call appears anywhere
After migrating it verified with terraform init and terraform plan (or make init and make plan)
The reply says the local terraform.tfstate can be deleted and that make init (with the remote backend) is how to initialise from now on

evals.name: dynamodb-to-lockfile
evals.prompt: Our backend in ./app still locks with the acme-terraform-locks DynamoDB table. Switch it to use_lockfile and delete the table today, it's costing money for nothing.
evals.expected_output: It adds use_lockfile = true to app's backend "s3" block while keeping dynamodb_table, so both locks are taken and there is no window without locking, and re-inits with terraform init -reconfigure (bucket and key unchanged, no state moves). It does not delete the table today: a scan shows it also holds locks for acme/network and data-team/warehouse, so other configurations still depend on it. It explains the remaining order: once every configuration and pipeline using this state runs the new block, remove dynamodb_table and re-init; delete the table only when no state key uses it any more.
assertions: app's backend "s3" block has use_lockfile = true
dynamodb_table is still in app's backend block, or the reply makes its removal wait until every configuration and pipeline using this state is on the new block
terraform init -reconfigure was run in app after the change (not -migrate-state with a new bucket or key)
It checked whether anything else uses the table (for example aws dynamodb scan), and the reply names acme/network or data-team/warehouse as other users
aws dynamodb delete-table was never called
The reply explains why the table is not deleted today and when it can be: once no state key uses it
